# Assignment

## Assignment {.fs70}

::: {.columns .pv4}
::: {.column width="60%"}
-   It is often useful to store data in [named objects]{.b .green}
    -   This makes the data easier to use and re-use
    -   This makes the code easier to write and read

::: {.fragment .mt1}
-   Which command is easier to follow?
    1.  Dial *7 8 5 8 6 4 0 8 4 1*
    2.  Call *Office Phone*
:::

::: {.fragment .mt1}
-   Named objects are created using [assignment]{.b .blue}
    -   Give a **name** then an **arrow** then the **data**
:::
:::

::: {.column .tc .pv5 width="40%"}
{{< lif "../../icons/contacts.json" trigger=hover colors=secondary:#2a76dd class=rc >}}

::: {.fragment}
`office <- 7858640841`
:::
:::
:::

## Assigning and Printing

```{r}
#| echo: true

# Store the value 2 under the name x
x <- 2

# Typing the name on its own prints the value
x
```

## Using an Object in Math

```{r}
#| echo: true

# Once x exists, it stands in for its value
x * 4

# Which is the same as writing it out
2 * 4
```

## Updating Requires Assignment

```{r}
#| echo: true

# Using x does not change it
x + 1

# x is still 2
x
```

```{r}
#| echo: true

# To update it, assign the result back to the name
x <- x + 1
x
```

## Using an Object More Than Once

```{r}
#| echo: true

# x can appear as many times as you like in one line
(10 + x - 1) / x
```

## Objects Can Create Other Objects

```{r}
#| echo: true

# The right-hand side can use objects that already exist
y <- 10 + x
y

# And a line can use several objects at once
y / x
```

# Naming

## Naming {.fs70}

::: {.columns .pv4}
::: {.column width="60%"}
-   Object names can [only include]{.b .blue}:
    -   Letters: `a-Z`
    -   Numbers: `0-9`
    -   Underscores: `_`
    -   Periods: `.`

::: {.fragment .mt1}
-   Additional Rules:
    -   Must [start with a letter or period]{.b .blue}
    -   Cannot contain spaces or dashes
    -   Cannot contain other symbols
    -   Names are case-sensitive (`age` ≠ `Age`)
:::
:::

::: {.column .tc .pv5 width="40%"}
{{< lif "../../icons/business_card.json" trigger=hover colors=secondary:#2a76dd class=rc >}}
:::
:::

## Good Names are a Balancing Act

```{r}
#| echo: true

x <- 93 # legal, but what is it?

rate <- 93 # too short to be clear

heart_rate_in_beats_per_minute <- 93 # too long to type

heart_rate_bpm <- 93 # just right
```

## Pitfall: No Spaces or Dashes

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
#| code-line-numbers: false

heart rate <- 93 # Error: unexpected symbol

heart-rate <- 93 # R reads this as heart - rate, not a name
```

::: aside
*Note.* These will not even run --- R cannot make sense of the line at all. Use an underscore instead: `heart_rate`.
:::

## Pitfall: No Special Symbols

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
#| code-line-numbers: false

age@time2 <- 12 # Error: @ means something else in R
```

```{r}
#| echo: true

age_time2 <- 12 # correct
age_time2
```

## Pitfall: Cannot Start with a Number or Underscore

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
#| code-line-numbers: false

1_heart_rate <- 93 # Error: unexpected input

_heart_rate <- 93 # Error: unexpected input
```

```{r}
#| echo: true

heart_rate_1 <- 93 # correct: the digit comes last
heart_rate_1
```

## Names are Case-Sensitive

```{r}
#| echo: true

heart_rate <- 93
Heart_rate <- 88

# These are two entirely different objects
heart_rate
Heart_rate
```

# Functions

## Functions {.fs70}

::: {.columns .pv4}
::: {.column width="60%"}
-   [Recipes]{.b .green} allow chefs to cook up tasty treats
    -   Recipes call for ingredients
    -   Recipes involve one or more steps
    -   Steps transform ingredients into treats

::: {.fragment .mt1}
-   [Functions]{.b .blue} are like *customizable* recipes
    -   Functions call for inputs ("arguments")
    -   Functions involve one or more lines of code
    -   Code transforms inputs into outputs
    -   Using functions requires parentheses (usually)
:::
:::

::: {.column .tc .pv5 width="40%"}
{{< lif "../../icons/blender.json" trigger=hover colors=secondary:#2a76dd class=rc >}}

::: {.fragment}
`out <- f(in1, in2)`
:::
:::
:::

## Functions Do a Task More Readably

::: {.f5}
`output <- function_name(input)`
:::

```{r}
#| echo: true

# The hard way
9 ^ (1 / 2)

# The readable way
x <- sqrt(9)
x
```

## Functions Can Transform Objects

```{r}
#| echo: true

y <- 9

# The input can be an object rather than a literal value
sqrt(y)
```

## Functions Can Transform Calculations

```{r}
#| echo: true

2 / 3

# The input can also be the result of a calculation
round(2 / 3)
```

## Arguments Customize a Function

::: {.f5}
`output <- function_name(argument, argument_name = argument_value)`
:::

```{r}
#| echo: true

round(2 / 3, digits = 2)

round(2 / 3, digits = 3)
```

## Some Arguments Have Defaults

```{r}
#| echo: true

# digits has a default value of 0, so this...
round(2 / 3)

# ...means exactly the same thing as this
round(2 / 3, digits = 0)
```

# Vectors

## Vectors {.fs70}

::: {.columns .pv4}
::: {.column width="60%"}
-   [Vectors]{.b .blue} combine similar objects into a collection
    -   *I like to imagine a train pulling multiple cars*<br />
    ![](../../img/traincar.png)
    -   A vector is one object with many sub-objects
    -   We refer to each sub-object as an [element]{.b .green}

::: {.fragment .mt1}
-   Some functions [transform each element]{.b .green} in turn
    -   *Double the amount of cargo in every train car*
:::

::: {.fragment .mt1}
-   Some functions [summarize across elements]{.b .green}
    -   *Calculate the total cargo across all train cars*
:::
:::

::: {.column .tc .pv5 width="40%"}
{{< lif "../../icons/old_train.json" trigger=hover colors=secondary:#2a76dd class=rc >}}

::: {.fragment}
`v <- c(1, 2, 3)`
:::

:::
:::


## Combining Elements into a Vector

::: {.f5}
`vector_name <- c(element1, element2, element3)`
:::

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
#| code-line-numbers: false

x <- 4 9 16 25 # Error: you must separate elements with commas
```

```{r}
#| echo: true

x <- c(4, 9, 16, 25)
x

y <- c(2, 3)
y
```

## Combining Vectors and Elements

```{r}
#| echo: true

# c() also joins whole vectors together
c(x, y)

# And vectors and single elements
c(x, y, 20)
```

## Math Transforms Each Element

```{r}
#| echo: true

x + 1

x * 3

# But as before, nothing is saved without assignment
x
```

## Some Functions Transform Each Element

```{r}
#| echo: true

sqrt(x)

log(x)
```

## Other Functions Summarize the Whole Vector

```{r}
#| echo: true

length(x)

sum(x)

mean(x)
```

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| error: true

average(x)
```

## Pitfall: Missing Values are Contagious

```{r}
#| echo: true

scores <- c(10, 12, 20, NA, 8)

# NA spreads: the mean depends on the value we do not have
mean(scores)

# Ask for the mean of the non-missing values instead
mean(scores, na.rm = TRUE)
```
